questions.request: Investigate the document Download operation in this Paperless revision. Explain how the requested document, the selected version or original/archive representation, and the authenticated user's authorization relate to the file returned. Identify the relevant control branches and whether selecting another version changes the resource that is authorized. Analyze ownership and object-grant branches without assuming that either is present. State precisely which source or deployment facts are missing.

The Download action delegates the requested document key to file_response, which first resolves the requested document and its root document. For a non-null request.user, the shown resolver checks owner-aware view permission on the root document; a failed check returns a forbidden response before file selection. A null request.user bypasses that check in this helper. file_response then selects an effective file document and chooses original versus archive representation, but the source bodies that define effective-version selection and final file serving are being selected for review and are not yet semantically closed. Consequently, this revision cannot yet establish from the current graph whether a selected alternate version is always tied to the authorized root, nor fully characterize the returned representation. questions.explanation: The Download entry delegates the requested document key and request context to file_response and returns that helper's response; missing-document exceptions are translated to Http404, so no file is returned on that branch (ev-aa429a725d3092cdd115). file_response resolves the requested document with deleted documents included, obtains its root document, and checks authorization before file selection. If resolution yields HttpResponseForbidden, file_response returns it without serving a file (ev-02e44f6c9deb225b1857; ev-990997ca1d3a5267e20b). For a non-null request.user, the resolver invokes owner-aware documents.view_document permission checking on the root document; a false result returns forbidden, while a true result permits resolution to continue. If request.user is None, this resolver skips that check and returns the requested and root documents. The actual principal value, owner relationship, and object-grant result are runtime or deployment facts not supplied here; the source shows the owner-aware helper call but its accepted semantic body is not closed in the current graph (ev-990997ca1d3a5267e20b; ev-458142315ae76eda187c). After successful resolution, _get_effective_file_doc returns the requested document directly when request_doc.root_document_id is non-null and no request version parameter is present; otherwise it delegates to _resolve_file_doc(root_doc, request). Thus the source shows that selecting a version can cause a different effective file document to be chosen, but the decisive _resolve_file_doc semantics are not available here, so this inquiry cannot establish whether every alternate version remains bound to the authorized root document or whether any alternate resource receives an independent authorization check (ev-a174e487981ce68cae7f; ev-1632637e8a259c495047). The selected effective document is then passed to serve_file. With original_requested(request) true, use_archive is false; otherwise use_archive is true only when the effective document has an archive version. serve_file reads archive_file and uses archive naming and PDF content type when use_archive is true; otherwise it reads source_file and uses the effective document's ordinary filename and MIME type, returning a FileResponse with the requested disposition and Content-Disposition header (ev-02e44f6c9deb225b1857; ev-ca6ea1cce1822f6ce320). Therefore the source establishes authorization on the root document before representation selection, and establishes that original versus archive changes the file representation of the effective document, not by itself the authorization object. It does not yet establish the complete version-to-resource binding or all ownership/object-grant outcomes.

paths.explanation: The path is source-bound through entry delegation, root-document resolution, effective-file selection, and serve_file, but remains unresolved because _resolve_file_doc and the accepted owner-aware permission-helper semantics are not closed. Known branches are: nonexistent requested document -> Http404/no file; forbidden root authorization result -> forbidden/no file; request.user=None -> this resolver skips the owner-aware check; non-null user with failed root view permission -> forbidden/no file; successful resolution -> effective document selection and file serving. The protected effect is reading and returning the effective document's source or archive bytes. The source does not prove that an alternate version is separately authorized or that it is always the same resource as the root-authorized document.
